episodes.168789: A severe thunderstorm developed in central Goshen County dropping quarter size hail near Yoder, south of Torrington early in the afternoon. Additionally, strong winds with a frontal passage moved through areas further west across southeast Wyoming wind-prone locations.
episodes.168790: Strong thunderstorms developing in far eastern Wyoming moved into the Nebraska Panhandle early in the afternoon on the 20th. A few storms became severe with strong winds causing tree damage near Bayard and large hail up to golf ball size.
episodes.169204: A long-lived supercell thunderstorm tracked across far northwestern South Dakota from southeastern Montana and northeastern Wyoming. The storm produced large hail and strong wind gusts across western and northern portions of Harding County.
episodes.169224: Thunderstorms caused gusty outflow or downburst winds.
episodes.169229: A severe thunderstorm tracked east-northeast through portions of northern Campbell County before weakening as it approached Crook County. The storm produced large hail north and west of Gillette.
episodes.169230: A line of severe thunderstorms developed across southwestern South Dakota and tracked east-northeast into central South Dakota. The storms produced wind gusts as high as 80 mph.
episodes.169233: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms tracked over the northern Black Hills area before weakening as it moved onto the plains. The storms produced wind gusts to 60 mph and small hail.
episodes.169545: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms produce gusty winds over the coastal waters.
episodes.169546: Afternoon thunderstorms produce minor flooding in North Fort Myers in Lee County.
episodes.169910: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced some large hail and strong winds.
episodes.169911: An isolated thunderstorm produced some severe hail in Dayton.
episodes.169912: An isolated thunderstorm produced some wind damage.
episodes.170117: A damaging wind event unfolded across west-central Minnesota during the evening of June 20 and into the overnight hours of June 21. Temperatures in the mid to upper 90s along with dew points in the mid to upper 60s created ample instability for thunderstorms to develop ahead of a cold front, once the cap weakened during the evening. Despite fairly muggy dewpoints, the hot surface temperatures created inverted-V soundings that were primed for damaging wind potential. Thunderstorms came in three waves during the evening, as marginal shear values prohibited any long-lived or well-organized thunderstorms across the area. Numerous wind gusts of 60-70 kts were measured across west-central Minnesota, along with widespread tree damage. One fatality occurred when a tree fell on a camper in Douglas County.
episodes.170218: A couple rounds of thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of an elongated area of low pressure during the evening of the 19th across central South Dakota, and then tracked north-northeast. Straight-line wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph were produced, including at three miles south of Bunker (70 mph), and five miles west-southwest of Mound City (70 mph).
episodes.170220: A cold front draped from the upper James River Valley down into south central South Dakota triggered a severe thunderstorm during the early afternoon across north central South Dakota, and then a more significant and widespread bowing line of thunderstorms from central into northeastern South Dakota during the evening. The environment featured hot temperatures in the 80s and 90s and muggy conditions. The main thunderstorm complex produced straight-line winds of 60 to 85 mph, including a measured gust of 85 mph three miles south of Bunker, 82 mph ten miles southwest of the Chantler Creek Rec area, 80 mph eighteen miles south of Seneca, and 79 mph at the Pierre Regional Airport. There were several reports of property damage including numerous uprooted or damaged trees.
episodes.170221: A cold front across South Dakota triggered a line of severe thunderstorms that moved into a favorable environment, with hot temperatures in the 90s and muggy conditions, across west central Minnesota during the late evening. Straight-line winds of generally 60 to 70 mph were produced, including a measured gust of 71 mph both near Odessa and Graceville.
episodes.170342: Scattered high-based thunderstorms tracked across northern and western portions of South Central Nebraska on this Monday afternoon and evening, prompting a few reports of marginally-severe wind gusts. This included 62 MPH measured by a mesonet station six miles south-southeast of Overton, and 59 MPH measured by the Ord Airport ASOS. Activity diminished by mid-evening with the gradual loss of daytime heating.||This event unfolded in a classic hot, deeply-mixed environment, and mainly affected areas west of a line from Greeley-Alma. Deep layer shear was on the weak side, around 25-30 knots, with mixed-layer CAPE values peaking between 500-1000 J/kg. Given the deep mixing in place, healthy DCAPE values of 1000-1500 J/kg developed, allowing for the potential for intense wind gusts with stronger storms.
episodes.170502: A cold front moved across Wyoming on June 20th. The front brought strong winds that were mixed down by showers. The strongest wind was reported in Natrona County where wind was high as 72 mph was reported along Wyoming Boulevard to the south of Casper. Near Buffalo, WY, a 61 mph wind gust was reported at the Johnson County Airport. The public reported small limbs snapped off trees and a few shingles blown off homes in the city of Buffalo.
episodes.170594: Thunderstorms developed during the early afternoon hours over the northern Nebraska Panhandle. These storms tracked east along a cold front into the late afternoon and evening hours across northern Nebraska. Severe thunderstorms were reported with hail up to 3 inches in diameter in northern Garden county and thunderstorm wind gusts of 80 to 90 MPH in Holt county. Numerous trees were reported down in O'Neill and portions of northern Holt county.
episodes.170651: A warm front lifted across the Northland during the early morning hours of the 20th bringing an unusually warm and moist airmass to the region creating very unstable conditions by the afternoon hours. During the late evening hours, a very strong low level jet ramped up and led to the development of storms across central Minnesota that moved to the northeast. Additional storms developed on the backside of the initial wave with the severe storm potential tapering off just before midnight. The storms primarily produced tree damage as they worked across the region, but there was some marginally severe hail as well.
episodes.170945: Scattered thunderstorms developed along and ahead of a cold front.  The airmass featured at least 1000 J/kg DCAPE and 40 knots of deep-layer shear parallel to the frontal boundary, which supported upscale growth and a transition toward damaging wind.
episodes.171040: Some scattered thunderstorms moved from the SW to the NE through the northwest TX Panhandle, then into the central OK Panhandle. These storms managed to produce some wind gusts in excess of 58 MPH both in the Texas Panhandle and again in the Oklahoma Panhandle.
episodes.171059: Two areas of severe weather developed during the evening hours. The first area was over south central North Dakota into the James River Valley along a surface trough which moved east. The second area started over southwest North Dakota and moved east along a frontal boundary. The strongest wind gust reported was 79 mph near Medina in Stutsman County, and the largest hail reported was the size of a tennis ball, which occurred near Haynes in Adams County.
episodes.171087: Two areas of thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and early evening hours. The first area was over south central North Dakota into the James River Valley along a slow moving frontal boundary. The second area was over southwest North Dakota ahead of a progressing surface trough. The largest reported hailstone was two inches in diameter, and fell in Dickey County. The strongest reported winds were estimated at 70 mph, which caused tree damage in LaMoure County. In addition, over the Dickinson area copious amounts of small hail fell, along with heavy rain. Although the largest hailstones were the size of a nickel, the hail piled up closing some streets and stranding some cars. The hail also combined with gusty winds to create hail drifts, some a few feet high.
episodes.171198: A potent upper level disturbance initially brought showers and thunderstorms to the region, but transitioned to a more stratiform event that produced many heavy rain reports.
episodes.171209: On June 20th, late afternoon thunderstorms developed in far southwestern Nebraska due to a surface trough moving through the region. One of these thunderstorms produced an estimated 70 mph wind gust.
episodes.171216: On June 20th, late afternoon thunderstorms developed in northwestern Kansas due to a surface trough moving through the region. These thunderstorms produced wind gusts up to 65 mph.
episodes.171500: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed along outflow boundaries in the southeast Gulf of Mexico, producing isolated gale-force wind gusts just outside Key West's Northwest Channel.
episodes.171531: Scattered summer thunderstorms resulted in a lightning strike that damaged a house.
episodes.171694: Isolated high based severe thunderstorms were observed.
episodes.171731: Scattered severe thunderstorms impacted portions of the southern Devils Lake Basin and the central Red River Valley. Hail and damaging wind gusts were reported, including one significant wind report over 70 mph.
episodes.171732: Severe thunderstorms formed during the afternoon, moving across the southern and central portions of the Red River Valley, then into west-central and northwest Minnesota. Wind gusts to 85 mph were reported, along with 2 tornadoes, and numerous other reports of hail and high wind damage.
episodes.171733: Severe thunderstorms formed during the afternoon, moving across the southern and central portions of the Red River Valley, then into west-central and northwest Minnesota. Wind gusts to 85 mph were reported, along with 2 tornadoes, and numerous other reports of hail and high wind damage.
episodes.171834: Multiple funnel clouds were reported near Tetonia.
